VBO:0200272.summary: Can de Chira dogs are responsive, disciplined workers with a strong interest in livestock and a close bond with their handlers. This regional herding type from the Aragonese Pyrenees moves sheep and cattle, with sheep traditionally handled without biting. Its Aragonese name describes a dog that turns the flock, reflecting the task at the heart of its history.
VBO:0200272.shortDescription: Responsive Pyrenean herders that work closely with handlers, turning sheep and cattle through Aragón’s mountain pastures.

sources.title: RSCE: Can de Chira — description and herding work
sources.evidence: The registry describes responsive, obedient and disciplined livestock workers, used with cattle and sheep, handling sheep without needing to bite. Its Aragonese name means a dog that turns the flock. Character is a normative first-party description, not an empirical guarantee.
